title: Mind and Body
summary: No war between a ghostly mind and a mechanical body. Reason is an attribute of the individual.

lessons.title: The war that is not there
lessons.objective: Name the false picture: a ghostly mind at war with a mechanical body.

exercises.prompt: Which picture does this unit reject?

choices.text: A ghostly mind at war with a mechanical body
Mind and body as allies inside one person
Reason as an attribute of the individual
A person with neither thought nor a body

feedback.note: The unit drops the story of a ghost fighting a machine. That split is the error, not a fact about people.

exercises.prompt: Match each half of the false picture to the role it is given.

pairs.right: A spirit that is not the person
A device the spirit must fight

feedback.note: Ghost, machine, and war are three parts of one mistaken picture.

exercises.prompt: Name the conflict this unit says is not real.

parts.text: between a ghostly mind and a mechanical body.

feedback.note: The claim is negative first: that war is not how mind and body stand.

exercises.prompt: Build the false picture this unit refuses.

feedback.note: Fighting is the rejected relation. Sharing one life is the alternative, not this sentence.

exercises.prompt: On this unit, the ghost-versus-machine story is what?

choices.text: A false picture of a person
The starting fact of human nature
A conflict you should try to win
The way reason works

feedback.note: The war is a picture to discard, not a duty and not a method.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to the side it names in the false picture.

feedback.note: Those three words are the whole rejected slogan: ghostly mind, mechanical body, war.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two caricatures.

feedback.note: Ghostly and mechanical are the two insults the false picture puts on mind and body.

exercises.prompt: What should you keep from this lesson?

choices.text: Refuse the war between ghost and machine
Choose the ghost and ignore the body
Treat the body as a machine you must obey
Split the person into two enemies

feedback.note: The lesson only asks you to drop the war. Later lessons say what stands in its place.

exercises.prompt: State the rejection in order.

feedback.note: The short form is no war between mind and body.

exercises.prompt: Which pairing matches the false picture?

choices.text: Ghostly mind, mechanical body
Reason, the individual
One person, one life
Attribute, not a second self

feedback.note: Only the ghost-and-machine pairing is the picture this lesson names as false.

lessons.title: One individual
lessons.objective: Hold mind and body as aspects of one individual, not two rivals sharing a life.

exercises.prompt: How many individuals are mind and body, on this unit?

choices.text: One individual
Two individuals at war
Neither is an individual
A crowd of minds in one body

feedback.note: Mind and body are not two persons. They are facts about one individual.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to the view it belongs to.

feedback.note: A truce still assumes two enemies. The unit says there is one individual.

exercises.prompt: Complete the count.

feedback.note: The number that matters here is one: one individual, not two combatants.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim about how many beings are involved.

feedback.note: They are one individual. Armies and truces belong to the rejected story.

exercises.prompt: What does this lesson refuse to say about mind and body?

choices.text: That they are two rivals sharing a life
That they are aspects of one individual
That they are the same person
That both are real

feedback.note: Both are real, and both are the same individual. The rival story is what goes.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to what it is in this lesson.

pairs.right: An aspect of the same individual

feedback.note: Neither mind nor body is a second self standing beside the individual.

exercises.prompt: Fill the contrast.

feedback.note: Aspects of one individual replaces rivals in a shared life.

exercises.prompt: Who has the mind and the body?

choices.text: One individual
A ghost that borrows a body
A group that thinks for its members
A machine that has no individual

feedback.note: The owner is the individual. A ghost, a crowd, or a bare machine is not a substitute.

exercises.prompt: Put the lesson sentence in order.

feedback.note: Having both is not hosting two enemies.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence fits this lesson?

choices.text: Mind and body are aspects of one individual
Mind and body are two armies under a truce
The mind is a tool the body happens to carry
The individual is neither mind nor body

feedback.note: Aspects of one individual is the claim. A truce, a carried tool, or a missing person is not.

lessons.title: Reason belongs to the person
lessons.objective: Place reason as an attribute of the individual, not of a spirit world or a crowd.

exercises.prompt: On this unit, what is reason?

choices.text: An attribute of the individual
A ghost that visits the body
A power that belongs only to a group
A spare part bolted onto a machine

feedback.note: Reason is an attribute of the individual. It is not a visitor, a group mind, or a bolt-on part.

exercises.prompt: Match each home for reason to the verdict.

pairs.right: Not the thinker in place of the person

feedback.note: Reason stays with the individual. A spirit world and a crowd are the wrong owners.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit line about reason.

feedback.note: Attribute names what reason is here: a feature of the individual, not a second being.

exercises.prompt: Build the positive claim about reason.

feedback.note: The owner in the sentence is the individual, not the crowd and not a ghost.

exercises.prompt: Can a crowd replace the individual as the bearer of reason?

choices.text: No. Reason is an attribute of the individual
Yes. Only groups really think
Only when the body is treated as a machine
Only if a ghost thinks for both

feedback.note: Moving reason to a crowd repeats the error of taking it off the individual.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to what it describes.

pairs.right: The one who has that attribute

feedback.note: Attribute, individual, and false owner are the three slots to keep straight.

exercises.prompt: Say who has reason, and what reason is.

feedback.note: The individual is the bearer. Attribute is the relation, not a weapon aimed at the body.

exercises.prompt: Which move keeps reason where this unit puts it?

choices.text: Leave it as an attribute of the individual
Lift it into a spirit world
Pool it into the crowd
Bolt it onto a mindless machine

feedback.note: Leaving reason with the individual is the whole of this lesson.

exercises.prompt: Reject the wrong owner in one line.

feedback.note: The crowd is not the bearer. The attribute stays with the individual.

exercises.prompt: Which pair states the unit correctly?

choices.text: No mind-body war; reason is the individual's attribute
Mind and body are at war; reason takes the ghost's side
The body is a machine; reason is optional
The group thinks; the individual only houses it

feedback.note: Both halves of the unit summary belong together: no war, and reason as the individual's attribute.

lessons.title: No ghostly mind
lessons.objective: Deny that the mind is a disembodied ghost occupying a body.

exercises.prompt: What is the mind, on this unit?

choices.text: Not a ghostly being apart from the individual
A soul that can live with no individual
A guest that occupies a machine
A cloud of thought shared by many bodies

feedback.note: Dropping the ghost means the mind is not a second being that merely occupies someone.

exercises.prompt: Match each ghost story to why it fails.

pairs.left: A mind apart from the person
pairs.right: Makes the mind a second being

pairs.left: A mind that only occupies a body

feedback.note: Apart, occupying, and floating all detach the mind from the individual.

exercises.prompt: Name what the mind is not.

feedback.note: Ghost is the word for a mind imagined as something other than the individual.

exercises.prompt: Build the denial.

feedback.note: The denial is direct: the mind is not a ghost.

exercises.prompt: Who thinks, if there is no ghostly mind?

choices.text: The individual
A spirit that uses the individual
Nobody; thinking is unreal
A machine with no attribute of reason

feedback.note: Removing the ghost does not remove thought. The individual is the one who thinks.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to its status.

feedback.note: The mind stays. Only the ghostly version is refused. Reason remains an attribute.

exercises.prompt: Fill both denials about a detached mind.

feedback.note: A ghost and a mind apart from the individual are the same mistake in two words.

exercises.prompt: After you drop the ghost, what remains true?

choices.text: Reason is still an attribute of the individual
There is no mind at all
The body must win the war
Thought floats free of any person

feedback.note: The ghost goes. The individual's attribute of reason stays.

exercises.prompt: Say who the thinker is.

feedback.note: Thinking without a ghost does not erase the individual or the body.

exercises.prompt: Which line is the lesson?

choices.text: No ghostly mind stands in for the individual
A soul thinks, and the individual only watches
Minds are unreal because ghosts are unreal
Many ghosts share one body

feedback.note: The lesson denies a stand-in ghost. It does not deny the mind of the individual.

lessons.title: No mechanical body
lessons.objective: Deny that the body is a mindless machine the mind must conquer.

exercises.prompt: What is the body, on this unit?

choices.text: Not a mechanical thing at war with a mind
A mindless engine the ghost must conquer
A prison built for a spirit
Optional equipment for reason

feedback.note: The body is not a machine set against the mind. Conquering it is the old war story.

exercises.prompt: Match each machine story to the error.

pairs.right: Strips the individual of an integrated life
Puts mind and body back at war
Makes the body something other than the person

feedback.note: Mindless, conquered, and merely ridden are three ways of turning the body into a machine.

exercises.prompt: Name the caricature of the body.

feedback.note: Machine is the caricature. The body is not an enemy device.

exercises.prompt: Build the denial about the body.

feedback.note: The body is not a machine. Calling it a ghost would mix up the two caricatures.

exercises.prompt: With the machine picture gone, how do mind and body stand?

choices.text: Together in one individual, not at war
The mind has finally defeated the body
The body has finally defeated the mind
They no longer belong to the same person

feedback.note: Ending the machine story does not crown a winner. It leaves one individual.

exercises.prompt: Match each closing claim to its point.

pairs.right: Not a ghost at war with that body

feedback.note: Those three claims are the unit: no machine, no ghostly war, reason as an attribute.

exercises.prompt: Close the unit in two words.

parts.text: , and reason is an attribute of the

feedback.note: The two words that hold the unit are war, denied, and individual, as the bearer of reason.

exercises.prompt: Does rejecting a mechanical body mean rejecting the body?

choices.text: No. It rejects only the machine caricature
Yes. Only the mind is real
Yes. A ghost does not need a body
Yes. The crowd replaces both

feedback.note: The body stays with the individual. What goes is the picture of it as a mindless machine.

exercises.prompt: State the whole unit in order.

feedback.note: No war of ghost and machine, and reason as the individual's attribute, is the unit in one line.

exercises.prompt: Which summary is this unit?

choices.text: No ghost-versus-machine war; reason is an attribute of the individual
Train the ghost to defeat the machine
Drop both mind and body and keep only a crowd
Keep the war, but call it peace

feedback.note: The summary is the refusal of the war plus reason as an attribute of the individual.
